results.reason: The memo never mentions the Delivery Date conflict between Schedule §1.1 (date goods ship from Supplier's plant) and MSA §1.3 (delivery at Rochester). It also never discusses the loss of remedies for transit delays.
The memo does not recommend conforming the Schedule's Delivery Date definition to the MSA. It also gives no order of precedence between the documents.

The memo identifies MSA §4.3 as covering all housings and similar components worldwide, against the Term Sheet's Series 7 / U.S. scope. It explains the blocking of non-U.S. plants and alternative suppliers, and recommends narrowing to Series 7 Housings for U.S. purchases.

The memo identifies §15.2 as letting Verdane assign freely, including to a competitor, while Harlow needs consent. It notes the supply and confidential Specifications risk. It recommends prior written consent, a bar on assignment to competitors, and a change-of-control termination right.

The memo identifies Amendment §2.1 and §2.2 as removing gross negligence and the IP indemnity from the cap exclusions, so those losses would be capped at 12 months' fees. It recommends rejecting the change and restoring the original exclusions.
The memo states that §11.1 caps liability at fees paid in the prior 12 months. It lists the original §11.2 exclusions as gross negligence, willful misconduct and the IP Indemnity.
The memo cites Term Sheet §3.1 (Series 7 Housings only, within the United States) and uses it as the baseline for comparing MSA §4.3.
The memo states New York law governs under MSA §16.1. It cites no cases or statutes, flags the public-policy point as needing confirmation, and lists assumptions and open facts.

The memo is structured as a practical memo to the partner. Each issue gives location, why it matters and a recommended fix, issues are prioritized, and there is an assumptions and open points section.
The memo expressly uses the Term Sheet only as evidence of the deal. It states that the 3-year term and 45-day payment terms are not defects.
Section cites appear accurate and the benefiting party is correctly identified. The New York public-policy point is flagged as needing confirmation, and no fabricated authority is cited.
